title: EU Regulatory Architecture and the Fund Value Chain
summary: Level-setting on investing, asset management and funds, how EU rules are made and layered with Member State requirements, and a framework for deciding which rules apply at each link of the value chain.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Level-setting on investing, asset management and funds, how EU rules are made and layered with Member State requirements, and a framework for deciding which rules apply at each link of the value chain.
Learning Objectives: Explain directives, regulations, technical standards, guidelines and Q&As and how they interact
Map the fund value chain from product and distribution to management, operations and administration
Determine which EU rules apply by asking what, who and how
Syllabus: What investing, asset management and an investment fund are
Level 1 to Level 3: the Commission, co-legislators, ESMA and national authorities
UCITS or AIF: the core classification and why managers choose each
Break-out: mapping supervisory risks to the value chain
Intended Audience: Supervisors, authorisation and policy staff at national competent authorities covering funds and asset managers
Compliance, legal, risk and product staff at UCITS management companies, AIFMs, investment managers and distributors
Directors, depositary and fund administration staff who need a working map of the EU fund rulebook
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of asset management, funds or their supervision is helpful. No legal background or prior knowledge of EU law is required.
Core Reading: Directive 2009/65/EC on undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (UCITS Directive)
Directive 2011/61/EU on Alternative Investment Fund Managers (AIFMD)
Directive (EU) 2024/927 amending the AIFMD and UCITS Directive on delegation, liquidity risk management, supervisory reporting, depositary services and loan origination (AIFMD II)
Regulation (EU) 2019/2088 on sustainability-related disclosures in the financial services sector (SFDR)
